texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/vid: Arsenal fall to a 2-0 defeat against a superior Lyon side in the Women's Champions League, dealing a blow to their hopes of automatic quarter-final qualification.
texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art:
Arsenal goalkeeper Misa Rodriguez made six saves but was beaten twice in defeat by Lyon
It is only 18 months since Arsenal tasted European glory, but they are not a team on many people's list of favourites for this season's Women's Champions League.
That is because not only have the Gunners disappointed across their opening 15 matches of the season, but also the elite teams in Europe seem to have gone up another level.
In the space of seven days, Arsenal have witnessed first hand what it takes to reach those heights - and the gap they must bridge.
Last week, they were resilient at Barcelona to earn a very respectable 1-1 draw, but were fortunate the Spanish side were not clinical with their chances at Camp Nou.
On Thursday night, they were outplayed at home in losing 2-0 to an excellent Lyon side , who look on course to match or better their runner-up finish from last season.
One point from such games could be pleasing - but that only shows the work Arsenal need to do to be considered one of the top teams in Europe.
French giants Lyon outclass Arsenal in Women's Champions League
Arsenal came into Thursday's defeat by Lyon off the back of a fifth successive Women's Super League draw at Emirates Stadium against London City Lionesses.
In contrast, Lyon have been flying domestically, winning all nine of their matches, scoring 49 goals, and then not conceding any in their unbeaten Champions League run.
Such form sets the pace and it was clear at Meadow Park that they were superior to Arsenal in every department.
Vibrant Germany international Jule Brand gave them the lead midway through the first half and Melchie Dumornay sealed the win with a powerful strike in the 57th minute.
Arsenal defender Leah Williamson said the "better team won the game" and manager Renee Slegers highlighted the difference in physicality between the teams.
"Compared to last year when we played Lyon [in the semi-finals], they are even better now. They have standout individual quality," Slegers said.
"They dominated in the first half. We had solutions for the second half and had more presence. We wore them down better but it still didn't lead to open chances."
Despite playing at right-back, Jule Brand had the third most touches in the Arsenal penalty area for Lyon (five) after striker Marie-Antoinette Katoto and fellow goalscorer Melchie Dumornay
Lyon had a 3.33 expected goals ratio on Thursday, serving up 23 shots to Arsenal's seven. They created six big chances and 14 of their shots were inside the box.
Dumornay oozed quality, midfielder Lily Yohannes showed composure and Brand was very impressive both defensively and going forward for Lyon, deployed in a new position.
Those individuals have benefitted from the expertise of former Barcelona manager Jonatan Giraldez, who joined in June 2025 - the month after Arsenal won the Champions League - and has now had the time he needed to impose his style.
As a result, Lyon have gone up another level and the gap between these two teams has widened by Arsenal's drop-off this season.
Slegers also said Arsenal had "prepared all we could" for the intensity that Lyon brought in London - but it still did not have an impact.
Asked how far off Lyon they currently are, Slegers said: "It's 2-0 today and they are better than us but it doesn't mean if we were to play them again soon, this season, that it would be the same game again.
"We saw moments where we did well and we know from the last couple of years we can hurt Lyon.
"But for today, their pace and physicality helped them get too much dominance in the game and that is one of their strengths. Then it became hard for us."
Arsenal have not yet qualified for the knockout stages of the Champions League
Williamson said Arsenal "know what they need to do to be better" and that they are aware of "where the gaps are" to Europe's elite.
They are already 12 points off the pace in the Women's Super League title race and are unlikely to qualify automatically for the Champions League quarter-finals.
"The level rises year on year. Everybody cops goals - we have to try not to and we have to create," said Williamson following the defeat by Lyon.
"We're all focused and we're all together. That's the most comforting thing for me - but this has been a tough period."
It has not all been bad despite disappointing results - and context is important.
Over a gruelling seven days, they have faced European holders Barcelona, WSL high-flyers London City Lionesses and record Champions League winners Lyon.
They showed grit and resilience out in Barcelona last week - traits that have not been on show enough for Arsenal this season, but are clearly there.
Players like Williamson, striker Alessia Russo and summer signings Georgia Stanway and Ona Batlle know what it takes to compete at the highest level.
Arsenal invested in the summer transfer window and brought in proven, experienced players, but that has not translated into results - yet.
Giraldez said time with his players has helped improve Lyon and perhaps that is what Arsenal need - patience.
"I think they are changing now. They made a good game against Barcelona and it's very difficult to go there and get a point," said Giraldez.
"The game against London City was much better. It's not just about them, but also about us. Now we have improved and play better football than last year.
"I think it is a matter of time [for Arsenal]. They have a good coach and good players. In general, they have all the ingredients to have a good season."

New Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino (right) worked with his full squad for the first time on Thursday
Manchester United fans have been given a unique and unexpected insight into Mauricio Pochettino's first training session after footage was captured by a drone flown next to the club's Carrington training ground.
Twelve minutes of the session was filmed by a drone operator and uploaded onto YouTube.
Pochettino and his players, who were split into three groups, are clearly visible, with the session filmed from a variety of angles and distances.
"For the people asking about legality. It is unrestricted airspace, meaning anyone can fly over it," said the drone operator.
"The drone remained in line of sight at all times, it didn't fly over anyone or even near anyone so was a perfectly legal flight going by the CAA rules that regulates drone usage.
"The drone is correctly labelled, and I hold all the relevant licences, public liability and insurance required. As for leaking team news/tactics, it was half an hour into the managers first training session, there are many media there so certainly won't be the only footage of training released."
The session was also filmed by United's own media channel, who regularly film club training sessions.
Civil Aviation Authority guidelines include the following warning: "If you use these devices where people can expect privacy, such as inside their home or garden, you're likely to be breaking data protection laws."
Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino (second right) hugs forward Bryan Mbeumo
There were 10 outfield players working with Pochettino, although it seems unlikely it will be the starting line-up for Sunday's trip to Liverpool.
While Harry Maguire, Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo are regular starters, Ayden Heaven and Andrey Santos have had less involvement, and neither Joshua Zirkzee nor Harry Amass have started a Premier League game this season. Jaume Camacho 17, who is yet to feature at senior level, was also with the group.
On an adjoining pitch, skipper Bruno Fernandes is shown in one group playing the 'rondos' game, where two players are in the middle trying to intercept the passes of the five players in a circle on the outside. Youngster Shea Lacey and last season's FA Youth Cup-winning skipper Dan Armer are also involved, along with England youth international Bendito Mantato.
Next to that is another group which includes more experienced players in Lisandro Martinez, Matthijs de Ligt, Youri Tielemans, Mason Mount, Leny Yoro, Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot.
The identical twins Jack and Tyler Fletcher are split between the two groups, with Pochettino's assistant Jesus Perez across both.
Not all the players were identifiable and United confirmed defender Patrick Dorgu was involved.

Senaryosunu yazdığı, yönettiği ve başrolünde oynadığı “Son Yemek” filminin galasında basın mensuplarının sorularını yanıtlayan Özcan Deniz, televizyon projelerine bir süre ara vermek istediğini açıkladı. Ünlü oyuncu, bu kararın ardında ailesine daha fazla vakit ayırma ve çocuğuyla ilgilenme isteğinin bulunduğunu söyledi. Deniz, açıklamasıyla bir süre yeni dizi projelerinde yer almayacağının sinyalini verdi.
Habertürk muhabiri Nazif Şahin Karpuz'un sorularını yanıtlayan Deniz, televizyona küs olmadığını ancak uzun yılların yorgunluğunu hissettiğini anlattı. Sanatçı, “Biraz artık kendime zaman ayırmak istiyorum. Çocuğumu büyütmek istiyorum” sözleriyle önümüzdeki dönemde önceliğinin ailesi olacağını dile getirdi.
Oyunculuk kariyeri boyunca çok sayıda televizyon projesinde yer alan Özcan Deniz, özellikle “Asmalı Konak” dizisinde canlandırdığı Seymen Karadağ karakteriyle geniş kitlelerce tanındı. Deniz, daha sonra “Haziran Gecesi”, “Kader”, “Aşk Yakar”, “Samanyolu”, “Bir Zamanlar Osmanlı: Kıyam”, “Karagül”, “Kaderimin Yazıldığı Gün”, “İstanbullu Gelin” ve “Seni Çok Bekledim” VE "Kızıl Goncalar" yapımlarında rol aldı.
Sanatçının son televizyon projelerinden biri ise 2023-2025 yılları arasında yayınlanan “Kızıl Goncalar” oldu. Dizide Doktor Levent Alkanlı karakterini canlandıran Deniz, televizyon kariyerine bir süre ara vererek ailesine ve kişisel yaşamına zaman ayırmayı planlıyor.
Filmin izleyiciyle buluşmasından heyecan duyduğunu belirten Deniz, son kararın her zaman seyirciye ait olduğunu vurguladı. Seyirciyi güldürmenin mi ağlatmanın mı daha zor olduğu sorusuna ağlatmanın çok daha zor olduğu yanıtını veren Deniz, filmin ana fikrini “Küçük dertler geveze, büyük dertler sessizdir” sözleriyle özetledi.
Özcan Deniz'in yaklaşık 3-4 yıldır üzerinde çalıştığı “Son Yemek”, 18 Kasım akşamı düzenlenen galanın ardından 19 Kasım'da izleyiciyle buluştu. Net Yapım ve Mahzen Media ortaklığıyla çekilen filmde Deniz, Bekir karakterine hayat verirken piyanist Sebahat rolünü Öykü Karayel üstleniyor. Çeyrek asra yayılan bir aşk hikâyesini anlatan filmin kadrosunda Nejat İşler, Tilbe Saran, Ceyda Düvenci, Helin Kandemir, Gonca Vuslateri ve Esra Ruşan da yer alıyor.
Uzun yıllardır hem müzik hem de oyunculuk kariyeriyle tanınan Özcan Deniz, son yıllarda senarist ve yönetmen kimliğiyle de öne çıktı. “Son Yemek”in müziklerine de katkı veren sanatçı, çekim sürecini kariyerinin en rahat setlerinden biri olarak tanımladı.

UEFA hand England suspended away ticket ban for "racist and/or discriminatory behaviour" during the 3-2 Nations League win over Spain in Madrid on Sunday; FA have also been fined £12,600
England have been given a suspended away ticket ban by UEFA for "racist and/or discriminatory behaviour" by their fans during the 3-2 win over Spain in Madrid.
The punishment is a one-match ban and is suspended for a "probationary period" of two years.
Sky Sports News understands the punishment is for anti-Catholic and anti-Irish chanting during the Nations League match.
A spokesperson for The FA told Sky Sports News : " We will not tolerate this unacceptable and deeply offensive chanting, and will work with the police who attend all England home and away matches to identify the perpetrators and take the necessary action."
The UK Football Policing Unit have also condemned the chanting from England fans in Spain. They are assisting the Spanish authorities with their enquiries.
A spokesperson for the UKFPU told Sky Sports News : "The UK Football Policing Unit has consistently made clear that we will not tolerate this type of unacceptable and deeply offensive chanting.
"These incidents have taken place in Spain and fall under the jurisdiction of the Spanish authorities and Spanish law, the UK Football Policing Unit will not be leading any investigation.
"However, we will work closely with the relevant Spanish authorities and provide any assistance necessary to support their enquiries and ensure those responsible are held accountable where appropriate.
"Discriminatory behaviour has no place in football or society, and we remain committed to working with our partners, in particular the FA both domestically and internationally, to challenge and address such conduct"

Arsenal register a single shot on target, which came in stoppage-time, as they were outclassed by Lyon at Meadow Park; Jule Brand and Melchie Dumornay scored in each half but the French side could easily have finished with more goals in what was a dominant performance
Arsenal’s hopes of automatic qualification to the Women’s Champions League quarter-finals are hanging by a thread after they were beaten 2-0 at home by a dominant Lyon in foggy conditions.
The French side, who beat Arsenal in the semi-finals last season, got the better of the Gunners again at Meadow Park on Thursday night with goals from Jule Brand and Melchie Dumornay in each half sealing the victory.
Arsenal barely laid a glove on Lyon - who are yet to concede a goal in this season's Champions League - and now sit eighth in the standings, three points adrift of fourth-placed Chelsea, after their first loss in five league phase matches.
Emily Fox registered Arsenal's only shot on target of the game deep in stoppage-time and the home side could easily have conceded a few more had Marie-Antoinette Katoto not spurned two big opportunities.
Arsenal were also indebted to their goalkeeper, Misa, who produced three big saves in the second half to keep out Tabitha Chawinga, Dumornay and Vicki Becho.
Renee Slegers' side, now without a win in three matches in all competitions, are relying on teams above them to drop points in the final round of matches to avoid having to face a play-off match to secure their passage to the quarter-finals.
Meanwhile, Lyon, who currently sit second in the table, have secured a top-four finish with a game to spare after picking up 13 points from five matches.
"Tough battle. Congratulations to Lyon who were better than us today. They play good football, physically strong in the duels, fast with the ball and without the ball.
"We had a tough time dealing with it in the first half. Second half we controlled the game better without creating clear-cut chances.
"But then you see how clinical Lyon were from their moments."
On her half-time team talk: "It was 1-0, so we were in the game. Like they had, we need moments as well. We are going to get moments and then how we are going to create it."
"The bigger picture here is that Arsenal have played the best two teams in this competition in two consecutive weeks and they've got just one point out of the two games.
"You have to admit the draw was very tough on them to get both Barcelona and Lyon, but it's also a harsh reality check.
"This Arsenal team won the Champions League just 18 months ago. Now, they're not quite up there with the European elites. Can they get back there anytime soon?"
"I like Renee but there has to come a time [when we question] why is it that all the players look out of form? Apart from Alessia Russo, how many of those players are actually performing?
"There has to come a point where you have to start questioning Renee. As much as I like Renee and everything she's done.
"Not to compare the two, but it feels like Michael Carrick at Man Utd where you feel like someone has taken the team so far but now what?
"We're all waiting for Arsenal to kick on. That tonight disappointed me because it looked flat."

Thomas Frank has admitted he has a point to prove on his return to management as he aims to steer Crystal Palace away from relegation trouble after taking over from Pierre Sage.
The Dane was confirmed as manager on Monday with Palace at the bottom of the table after 10 matches having conceded 24 goals – the most in the Premier League. They face a crucial trip to Coventry on Saturday and Frank said he had been “surprised about how good it feels” after returning to work for the first time since being sacked by ­ Tottenham in February .
The 53-year-old spent most of the intervening period travelling, working as a pundit at the World Cup and taking in trips to Japan, Australia and his native Denmark, where he was visiting friends and family when he received the SOS call from Palace last week. Frank previously spent seven years in charge of Brentford but left Spurs after just eight months with a win ratio of 34.2% – the worst of any permanent manager in the club’s history. He believes he has learned from that experience.
“I think you’ve all got an ego,” he said. “Some are better at controlling it than others. For me, it’s not the critics. It’s more what I can bring myself, what I can learn, what I can prove, how I can get better. I think that’s the big thing.
“In this world there’s a lot of clever people out there. But they only know a 10th of the truth. And that’s a 10th of the truth at Brentford and a 10th of the truth at Tottenham. That’s just the way it is – if you can’t handle that as a coach or a player or whatever, then you shouldn’t be in this business. I’m just very happy to be back in the game, very happy to be in a fantastic club, at Palace, where you walk in the door and you just feel the energy. You feel the people. It just feels good.”
Frank said he is planning to pick Roy Hodgson’s brains in the coming days after recalling a conversation they had when the former England and Palace manager was still at Selhurst Park.
“I was thinking, does it ever go away? The worry, do you get more relaxed about everything?” he asked Hodgson. “‘No chance, it’s impossible.’ I thought it would have been a little bit easier with age and experience. But in a way can’t help ourselves. I know what I want and the direction we should go in.”
Justin Cochrane – one of Thomas Tuchel’s assistants for England – has joined as first-team coach and took his first session with Palace on Monday less than 24 hours after the Nations League victory over Spain in Madrid. He is expected to be joined on Palace’s backroom staff by Bernardo Cueva, with Frank confirming that a deal with Chelsea is “very close” for the Mexican. Both worked with Frank at Brentford, where he spent almost nine years as an assistant and then manager. He is also hoping to add Andreas Georgson from Tottenham, who has been credited for his prowess on set-pieces: an area that Palace have struggled with for some time.
But asked whether he will be judged on the perception that his success at Brentford was based on the model that has allowed his successor, Keith Andrews, to thrive since taking over, Frank was not impressed. “Put it this way, I think it was pretty important in terms of building that model,” he said.

Thomas Frank replaces Frenchman Pierre Sage at Crystal Palace
Thomas Frank is happy to be "back in the circus" after speaking at his first news conference as Crystal Palace manager.
The 53-year-old, who was appointed on a two-and-a-half-year deal on Monday, has been out of worked since he was sacked by Tottenham in February, less than eight months after taking the job.
But, rather than dwell on that disappointment, Frank hopes to use it as a learning exeprience as he attempts to improve Palace's fortunes and lift them off the bottom of the Premier League table.
"If you don't learn from any of your jobs, I don't think you reflect, I don't think you improve, and I don't think you get better," said Frank.
"Of course there's a lot of things I have been reflecting over. The details, that will be for another time, but I can say I've learned, definitely."
The Dane said he could easily have extended his break from football, which he used to travel to Japan and Australia, as well as "visiting friends and family, eating too well [and] drinking too much wine" back in his homeland.
"I was very aware I didn't want to do anything in the summer. I put a statement out there, I needed more time," he added.
"I can actually, honestly say I would have been fine if it was three, four, five, six, seven months more, because it's good to be back in the circus, but it's also unbelievably good not to be in, especially if you enjoy life, which I do.
"I was spending time with family and friends and doing all that, but I think the club, the way Palace is, how well Steve Parish especially spoke about the club and ideas, Matt Hobbs and Iain Moody and these guys, too, helped convince me it was a good idea.
"I'm a little bit surprised by this feeling I have in the body, how good it feels."
Frank's Palace reign begins with a trip to Coventry City on Saturday (15:00 GMT) and he says he returns to the dugout unbruised despite the way his stint at Spurs ended.
"I think we all have an ego," the former Brentford boss said. "Some are better at controlling it than others. For me, it's not the critics, it's more what I can learn, what I can prove, how I can get better.
"There's a lot of clever people out there, but the interesting thing is they only know 10 per cent of the truth. That's a tenth of the truth at Brentford , there's a tenth of the truth at Tottenham , and that's just the way it is.
"If you can't handle that as a coach or a player, then you shouldn't be in this business, and I'm very happy to be back in the game."
Why Frank at Tottenham was a gamble that ended in bitter failure

Frick has managed Vaduz and Luzern in the Swiss Super League
Aberdeen head coach Mario Frick says his track record proves he can produce exciting football - but for now a back-to-basics approach is required to save the Dons' season.
The 52-year-old arrived in the Granite City on a two-and-a-half year deal earlier this week to replace Stephen Robinson, who was sacked with the team second bottom of the Scottish Premiership.
Frick, who left Luzern in the summer after nearly five years in charge, has already identified a key problem he must solve quickly.
"I am known for high-scoring clubs. Twice with Vaduz we had the highest scoring record and last year with Lucerne, 76 goals," he said.
"I think Aberdeen is lacking goals [12 in 12 league games] so I am here to change that. On Thursday morning for the first time we did our attacking patterns and we have to improve now - we need time but we don't have it.
"More important now is to show the basics - body language, being willing to work, aggression, intensity - that is what I want to see on Saturday in Kilmarnock."
His first game in charge is a real baptism of fire for the Swiss-born former Liechtenstein player.
Defeat for the Dons would mean they replace their Ayrshire hosts at the bottom of the table.
The recent cycle of instability at Aberdeen is highlighted by the fact Frick - who was capped 125 times - has become their seventh permanent manager in six years.
But he is not daunted by recent history or by Aberdeen's situation - and sees similarities between the job he faces at Pittodrie and the one he inherited at Luzern in December 2021.
"I have had a very long career as a professional so I know the pressure. I am always an optimist and I know what I can do," he said.
"Luzern were at the bottom of the table with 18 matches and 11 points and the whole environment was sad and we saved them, so I am pretty sure we can do this also here.
"I am very ambitious. Now it is very important to get out of this situation but we want to go in the top six."
Across almost three decades of working in the north-east of Scotland, I have seen many Aberdeen managers come - and go. In fact, far too many to name check.
From this side of the microphone, first impressions are always intriguing - and not always an accurate barometer for how things will play out.
For example, I watched Neil Warnock cut an impressive figure at his unveiling in February 2024 and look how that worked out.
Well, having attended his maiden Pittodrie press conference, and observed him briefly at training this morning at Cormack Park - he exudes a calm authority.
He gives off the vibe of someone who knows where he wants to go, how he wants to get there and I suspect will probably not suffer fools gladly on his way to trying to achieving those ends.
Once both parties get to know each other a bit better, I also get the impression he will quickly command respect from the dressing room.
Frick appears to be a straight talker, and pretty clear in what he wants to get across.
While that obviously bodes well from a journalist's point of view, more importantly it could be crucial for the players as he looks to quickly deliver a winning formula that he, and the fans, hope can get the team moving back up the Premiership table over the coming months.
"With a manager change there is still a chance for every player to prove themselves, a new chance for everybody.
"To be honest I was really surprised with the first training session. It was brilliant and I saw a lot of quality.
"The facilities are paradise, it is incredible. It is better than in Switzerland so for me it is the next step. I am very happy to be here. I am very thankful to Adrian [Bevington, chief executive], Lutz [Pfannenstiel, sporting director], Mr Cormack [Dave, chairman], and the whole board."
"For eight years I have been a professional coach with only two clubs.
"Then I felt it is time for the next step. I waited for five months for this next step and when Lutz called me on Monday after the Hibs game I was excited from the first moment.
"I am really, really happy to be here because it is such a big club, such a famous club, a historic club, I am just proud to be here."
"Heavy metal, that is high-pressing, that is counter-pressing, vertical play, creating many goalscoring chances, that is heavy metal.
"In the next two weeks we have five games so I am just getting to know the new team and I have to make some very difficult decisions. But I am an optimist and I think we can do very well."

90'lı yıllara şarkılarıyla damga vuran Pınar Aylin , kızı Maya Tokatlıoğlu ile birlikte “Aşk Tesadüfleri Sever” filminin galasına katıldı. Uzun süredir gözlerden uzak olan Maya'nın son hali gündem olurken, annesini boyuyla geride bırakması da gözlerden kaçmadı.
Bir dönemin sevilen pop müziği sanatçılarından Pınar Aylin , galada 24 yaşındaki kızı Maya ile birlikte objektiflere poz verdi. Anne-kızın şaşırtan benzerliği öne çıkarken, Maya'nın büyümüş hali büyük ilgi gördü.
Pınar Aylin ile kızı Maya'nın yan yana kareleri kısa sürede çok konuşulanlar arasına girdi. İkilinin arasındaki benzerliği görenler “İkizini doğurmuş” yorumlarında bulunurken, Maya'nın annesinden uzun boylu olması da gecenin en çok konuşulan ayrıntılarından biri oldu.
Maya Tokatlıoğlu, Pınar Aylin'in eski eşi Mert Tokatlıoğlu ile evliliğinden 2002 yılında dünyaya gelmişti.

Clubs rallied behind the Premier League’s leadership in a key vote on Thursday, overwhelmingly backing new rules that would protect the chief executive, Richard Masters, from potentially damaging lawsuits.
A vote to expand the legal indemnity afforded to Premier League directors was won 18-2 at a shareholders’ meeting in central London, granting Masters and other figures greater protection in the event they were subjected to legal action as a consequence of doing their job.
Manchester City are understood to be one of two clubs to vote against the extension of indemnity, and one unnamed side spoke out at length against the measures during the meeting. The other vote against was by Nottingham Forest, who felt insufficient time had been granted to consider the proposal.
The rule change follows reports that the organisation’s leadership may be named in possible legal action by City’s Abu Dhabi sponsors, who have claimed their reputations were damaged as a result of the excoriating verdict of an independent commission regarding City’s breaches of the league’s financial rules. City have appealed against the verdict.
This week the Abu Dhabi telecommunications giant and City sponsor Etisalat released a statement describing the contents of the verdict as “entirely false and defamatory”. Referring to the independent commission’s report as “the published findings of the English Premier League”, Etisalat said it was “actively considering all options relating to its rights and associated legal remedies in this matter”.
The details of any increase of indemnity, including who would cover any potential costs, were not discussed in the meeting.
The chief refereeing officer of Pro Ref, Howard Webb, attended and came under sustained questioning from club executives over recent referee and video assistant referee failures.
A report by the independent key match incidents panel this week found there had been two serious mistakes that were not corrected by the VAR during the most recent round of matches. Webb is understood to have acknowledged that performance in matchday 10 had been “poor” but argued that apart from that weekend, key metrics on decision-making had been trending in the right direction this season.
The Premier League has confirmed next season will begin on Friday 13 August and finish on 21 May. It said players would have 75 “clear days” of break at the end of the current season.

Bruno Guimarães to feel the heat on Tyneside, Alex Scott’s return further cheers Cherries and Manchester City face favourite whipping boys
After three Premier League defeats on the spin, Manchester City need something or someone to come along and put some pep in their step, and Fulham look like just the thing – after all, in the past 15 years these teams have played 20 times in all competitions, and City have won precisely 20 of those games. Their current run of 17 successive league wins against Fulham is the longest run of victories by one club against a single opponent in English top-flight history. It is a reflection of the changing realities of English football, and the gulf that has opened between the teams that dominate it and those who seek to challenge them, that of the top 10 such runs all but one occurred in whole or in part after 2010 and six of them have been achieved by Sheikh Mansour’s Manchester City, with Chelsea responsible for another two, Manchester United one, and Portsmouth’s postwar, 13-game supremacy over Everton – a wild ride that included two 5-0s, a 5-1, a 6-3 and a 7-0 – the anomaly. Simon Burnton
Positivity surrounds Aston Villa despite them failing to win in four matches, the last of which ended in agonising fashion; they had to settle for a 4-4 draw at Manchester United after twice squandering a two-goal advantage. Villa should have managed the final minutes better, but a home date with Sunderland presents an opportunity to return to winning ways. Unai Emery needs to eliminate the defensive naivety that has blighted some performances and the expected absence of Matty Cash, this time owing to concussion sustained on Poland duty, would deny the Villa manager his preferred defensive lineup. This fixture threw up a classic last season, Tammy Abraham scoring a stoppage-time winner to extend the visitors’ miserable record at Villa Park. Sunderland have won on only two of their past 17 league visits, their last victory coming in 2011 courtesy of the former Villa loanee Phil Bardsley. Ben Fisher
The last time Alex Scott played for Bournemouth, Marco Rose was yet to taste victory in the Premier League. When the 23-year-old returns to midfield he will do so with the team in a totally different place. Bournemouth have racked up eight straight wins in all competitions before hosting Nottingham Forest on Saturday and Scott, who has been able to build his fitness during the international break after a thigh problem, may have to wait his turn owing to the form of Tyler Adams and Ryan Christie. If Rose opts for momentum, then Eli Junior Kroupi, fresh from scoring his first France goal, could make his first start of the season after sustaining a freak foot injury in pre-season. Bournemouth have hardly been short of firepower, though, with Evanilson scoring seven goals in his past eight games. BF
Chelsea left Wearside battered and bruised after being pushed around by Brian Brobbey. The Sunderland forward bullied Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill, who had to be substituted at half-time, and won the game’s decisive penalty with a solo run that left Xabi Alonso angry with his side’s powderpuff defending. Alonso insisted Chelsea had prepared for Brobbey’s threat; the Chelsea manager will hope they are better at putting the plan into practice when they face another target man on Saturday. Leeds head to Stamford Bridge and will look to Dominic Calvert-Lewin, fresh from helping England get over the line against Spain last weekend, to unnerve Alonso’s defenders. Jacob Steinberg
Thomas Frank’s first assessment of his new charges after taking over at Crystal Palace this week included the nuggets that “we’re conceding too many goals … we need to work on the defensive side of things with principles, attitude, everything regarding that”, and in particular “we need to work on the set pieces, that’s key”. If he can’t inspire an immediate improvement this is where this match could be decided, being as it is an encounter between the league’s worst set-piece defenders – no one comes close to the 67 shots and xG of 7.44 coughed up by Palace at restarts – and the best. Though Coventry have let in one goal from set pieces, and neither Brentford nor Liverpool have shipped any, the hosts’ set-piece xG of 1.65 is a league low, and they were equally outstanding from dead-ball situations in the Championship last season. The home side will be boosted by the return of the 6ft 4in defender Bobby Thomas, who, despite a calf injury that meant he missed the last two games and the final third of the one before that, has still made more clearances than any other Coventry player. SB
It may have been a slightly strange week for Tottenham fans. They have watched as their former managers Mauricio Pochettino and Thomas Frank have been installed at Manchester United and Crystal Palace respectively, while their current head coach, Roberto De Zerbi, picked up the Premier League’s manager of the month award for October. That is reflective of the improvement De Zerbi has overseen in recent weeks, with Spurs happy to move forward with the Italian and avoid the chaos enveloping some of their rivals. The long-held assumption among some connected to Tottenham that Pochettino would one day return to save the club must now be banished; De Zerbi needs full buy-in from everyone to build his project. That’s the only way Spurs can ensure they steer clear of future crises. Dominic Booth
With the temperature in Newcastle forecast to dip to 0C at kick-off, Matthias Jaissle is perhaps hoping that his team’s guests from north London (where a balmy 9C is predicted at 5.30pm) freeze in the Tyneside chill. Otherwise it is hard to envisage his young side overcoming a formidable looking Arsenal on a day when Newcastle’s head coach seeks what would be only his second win in seven games. Home fans will not merely be hurt by the sight of their much-missed former captain Bruno Guimarães wearing Arsenal colours but decidedly nervous about a fixture that precedes a run of tricky engagements involving a trip to Brighton and home dates with Manchester United and Sunderland . Jaissle’s cause could be helped should Mikel Arteta name Guimarães in his starting XI and the crowd respond to the once adored Brazilian’s defection by creating the sort of hostile atmosphere that might just galvanise a Newcastle team expected to contain the former Arsenal midfielder Joe Willock. Meanwhile Jaissle’s defence must be mindful of the threat posed by another Newcastle old boy in Mikel Merino. Louise Taylor
Brighton are out to prove their early-season form has been no fluke and the fixture list for November and December looks promising for their chances of retaining their lofty position. Hull, having started the season with back-to-back league victories, now appear vulnerable and have not won since that August burst. Brighton follow the trip to Humberside with a home game against Universitatea Craiova in the Conference League, then host Newcastle, and face none of the big six until a visit to Tottenham on 29 December. With Brighton having won seven of their 10 league games, tentative talk of a title challenge may not seem so fanciful come Christmas. The challenge tactically for Fabian Hürzeler’s men will be to deal with the tag of favourites for most of their upcoming games, with teams perhaps starting to wise up to Brighton’s high-pressing, vertical style. DB
And so it starts all over again. Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager in 13 years – not forgetting the interim spells of Ryan Giggs, Michael Carrick, Ralf Rangnick and Darren Fletcher – was impressively quick to commit to the cause when taking a private jet from Cincinnati to Manchester immediately after his final game as USA head coach. Mauricio Pochettino needs his new, floundering team to reciprocate at Anfield. United have conceded four times in the first four minutes of a game this season, seven goals in the opening 17 minutes in total, and will have had littl…

Arsenal’s hopes of earning automatic progression to the Champions League quarter-finals were dashed by OL Lyonnes, as the French side continued their statement form in Europe.
Goals in either half from Jule Brand and Melchie Dumornay were the ­difference at Meadow Park and Lyonnes are joint-top of the table and still yet to concede in the league phase with one game remaining.
It feels like Lyonnes are playing with a fire and intensity fuelled by their loss to Barcelona in May’s Champions League final. They look a more formidable, coherent and hungry side on a mission to end a four-year run without lifting the trophy they won eight times in a 12-year period between 2011 and 2022.
“We are already at a better level for sure,” said the Lyonnes manager ­Jonatan Giráldez. “Sometimes you just need time. We had nine new ­players last season and I was new too as the coach. I think we have improved the rhythm of the game and have identified positions better and are staying more compact. The most important thing is speaking the same language in possession and out possession.”
The visit of the eight-time ­European champions was always going to be challenging for the ­Gunners and based on current form getting a result would be even tougher. Last season’s runners-up had scored 20 goals without conceding in their first four Champions League matches prior to their trip to Borehamwood and scored 49 in their nine Première Ligue games.
The lack of competitiveness in the France top flight also meant they were able to rotate heavily at the weekend between their two European games. Giráldez made 11 changes for their 1-0 defeat of Saint-Malo on Saturday before returning to his first-choice lineup against the 2025 Champions League winners .
Clàudia Pina scored a hat-trick as Barcelona thrashed Servette 6-0 to go top of the Women’s Champions League standings. While Lyon were winning 2-0 at Arsenal , Barça edged clear at the top on goal difference as they dismantled their Swiss visitors.
Aitana Bonmatí fired in the opener in the 19th minute and then turned provider for Pina to drill home her first goal.
Esmee Brugts headed in a third in the 32nd minute, and Barça had their fourth just after the hour, with Caroline Graham Hansen hitting an emphatic penalty after Bénédicte Simon fouled Brugts.
Pina got her second in the 77th minute and tucked in from Brugts’s pull-back to complete her hat-trick late on.
Bayern Munich are two points behind after cruising to a 4-0 win over Austria Vienna . Klara Buhl headed the visitors in front after 27 minutes before Pernille Harder doubled the lead in first-half stoppage time.
Alara Sehitler’s stunning strike made it 3-0 with 15 minutes to go before Sophie Proost added a fourth in stoppage time.
Sofia Jahnukainen struck in stoppage time as Roma snatched a 3-2 win away to Benfica . Kayleigh van Dooren twice put the Italians in front, but her first goal was cancelled out by a thunderbolt from Caroline Møller, with Flourish Sabastine equalising after her second.
Paris FC got their first win of the competition, beating HB Køge 2-1 thanks to Célina Ould Hocine’s late penalty. Catherine Paulson fired the visitors in front 10 minutes in, but Sheika Scott bundled in a rebound to bring Paris level before the break. Press Association
Arsenal were not afforded the ­luxury of an easy league match after their battling 1-1 draw against ­Barcelona last week , playing a critical and tricky game against London City Lionesses , which also ended 1-1. Renée Slegers made two changes to the team that hosted ambitious London City, with Ona Batlle ­having picked up a knock Taylor Hinds played at left-back and Kyra Cooney-Cross started ahead of Kim Little.
They had their backs against the wall at a bitterly cold Meadow Park, as Giráldez’s galacticos controlled the game. The away team had almost 69% possession in the first half and amassed 12 shots to Arsenal’s one.
The surprise was that Lyonnes were not further ahead at the break, with Brand’s 24th-minute goal the difference, the full-back sweeping in Vicki Bècho’s ball from the right.
Brand was back to haunt the ­Gunners, having scored in both legs of last season’s semi-final between the two teams, with the French side progressing to face Barcelona in the final with a 4-3 aggregate win.
Arsenal were better after the break, but Lyonnes soaked up brief spells of Arsenal pressure, Marie-Antoinette Katoto the only player left forward as they banked back and crowded the box to give the home players few options.
They increased their margin and dampened the mood soon after Arsenal’s brightest period, Tabitha Chawinga’s cross from the left was collected by Katoto and the France forward laid the ball off for Dumornay who took a touch before powering the ball into the roof of the net.
It was an emphatic and unstoppable finish from one of the best players in the world as a mist lowered over the pitch.
“Congratulations to Lyonnes, they were better than us today,” said Slegers. “If you look at the block we’ve had, the challenges we’ve had with the run of games – ­Liverpool and Barcelona away, ­London City who are among one of the top teams in the WSL right now and Lyon, who are even better than last year – it’s a lot of games against strong teams with a short turnaround because Lyon were better than us.”
Arsenal need to quickly move on, with West Ham their last game before the international break. They had needed a win to have any serious chance of earning a place in top four, avoiding a quarter-final playoff place.
They now sit eighth and will face Inter in their final league phase match in December, with the Italians needing a win to keep any hopes of a playoff place alive. That will not be easy, but a seeded playoff place is in Arsenal’s hands, if they want it.

Gündemi BBC Türkçe'den takip etmek artık WhatsApp'ta da mümkün. Haberlerimizin doğrudan telefonunuza gelmesi için tıklayın.
Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan emeklilerin ekonomik durumunun iyileştirilmesi için yapılacak düzenlemenin yılbaşından önce hayata geçirileceğini söyledi.
AKP Meclis Grup Toplantısı'nda konuşan Erdoğan, "17 milyonu aşkın emeklimizin tamamını kapsayan bir iyileştirmeyi yüce meclisimizin de desteğiyle sene başından önce hayata geçireceğiz" dedi.
Erdoğan, "Yaş ve prim gün sayısına göre adalet ve hakkaniyeti merkeze alan bir yaklaşımla meseleyi tüm boyutlarıyla değerlendiriyoruz" diye konuştu.
Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek TBMM Plan ve Bütçe Komisyonu'nda yaptığı açıklamada, teknik hazırlıkların Aralık ayında tamamlanmasını ve teklifin bütçe görüşmelerinin ardından Meclis'e sunulmasının beklendiğini söylemişti.
Mehmet Şimşek, bakanlığının 2027 bütçesi görüşmeleri sırasında, aylık artışının emeklinin yaşına ve prim günü sayısına göre farklılaşabileceğini belirtmişti.
Şimşek, seyyanen artış seçeneğinin uygulanması halinde de bu ölçütlerin gözetileceğini kaydetmişti.
Yaş ve prim günü için hangi eşiklerin esas alınacağı, bunların aylığa nasıl yansıyacağı henüz açıklanmadı.
AKP kaynaklarının daha önce BBC Türkçe' ye verdiği bilgiye göre yıl sonuna kadar yapılacak düzenlemede, emeklilere normal yıllık zammın yanı sıra, "refah payı" veya "seyyanen zam" seçeneği masada.
Ancak emekli maaşlarına yapılacak iyileştirmenin miktarında yaş, çalışma durumu, konut sahipliği veya hane geliri gibi kriterlerin esas alınması seçeneği değerlendiriliyor.
Ayrıca rutin enflasyon zammına ek olarak refah payı verilmesi, bunun yanı sıra bazı emekli gruplarına farklı oranlarda iyileştirme yapılması değerlendiriliyor.
Ancak bu seçeneklerin henüz kesinleşmiş bir düzenleme olmadığına dikkat çekiliyor.
AKP'de, yapılacak iyileştirmenin hangi kriterlere göre yapılacağı konusunda farklı seçenekler değerlendiriliyor.
Üst düzey bir parti yetkilisinin verdiği bilgiye göre ek iyileştirmelerin belirlenmesinde yaş kriterinin öne çıkması bekleniyor.
Bu kapsamda, 65 yaş ve üzerindeki emeklilere daha fazla destek verilmesi seçeneği üzerinde duruluyor.
AKP kaynakları, yaş sınırının belirlenmesinde emeklilerin çalışma hayatında kalabilme durumunun dikkate alındığını söylüyor.
Buna göre, 65 yaşın altındaki bazı emeklilerin çalışmaya devam ederek emekli maaşlarına ek gelir elde edebildiği, daha ileri yaştaki emeklilerin ise çalışma hayatında yer alma imkânlarının sınırlı olduğuna dikkat çekiliyor.
Ancak sınırın 60 yaşa çekilmesi seçeneğinin de değerlendirildiği belirtiliyor.
Düzenlemede yaşın yanı sıra emeklilerin ekonomik koşullarının da dikkate alınması gündemde.
AKP kaynaklarının verdiği bilgilere göre, değerlendirmede şu kriterler öne çıkıyor:
Bu kriterlerin nasıl bir yöntemle uygulanacağı ve emeklilerin hangi gruplara ayrılacağı henüz netleşmiş değil.
Dolayısıyla yaş, konut sahipliği veya gelir durumunun maaşlara yapılacak iyileştirmeyi hangi ölçüde etkileyeceği konusunda kesinleşmiş bir çerçeve bulunmuyor.
AKP kurmayları, emeklilerin ekonomik koşullarına ilişkin kapsamlı bir araştırma yürüttüklerini söylüyor.
Parti kaynaklarının aktardığı verilere göre, yıl sonunda toplam emekli sayısının 18 milyona ulaşması bekleniyor.
En düşük emekli aylığı olan 23 bin 552 TL'yi alanların sayısının ise 5 milyon 17 bin olduğu, bu gruptakilerin yaklaşık yarısının 65 yaş ve üzerinde olduğu belirtiliyor.
Bu veriler, olası bir düzenlemede yaş ve gelir kriterlerinin hangi grupları etkileyebileceği açısından önem taşıyor.
Ancak en düşük aylığı alan emeklilerin tamamının düzenlemeden nasıl yararlanacağına ilişkin henüz açıklanmış bir karar bulunmuyor.
AKP kaynakları, kamuoyunda EYT benzeri bir modelle tartışılan kademeli emeklilik düzenlemesinin şu aşamada gündemlerinde olmadığını da söylüyor.
Parti kaynaklarına göre, böyle bir düzenlemenin bütçeye ek yük getireceği ve mevcut koşullarda sürdürülebilir olmayacağı değerlendiriliyor.

Ukraine great Andriy Shevchenko has accused Mykhailo Mudryk's representatives of repeatedly asking for an employee of the country's football federation to "falsely" take the blame for the winger's positive drugs test.
Tottenham winger Mudryk, who is on a season-long loan from Chelsea , was suspended from November 2024 until July 2026 after testing positive for the banned substance meldonium.
The 25-year-old said he blames the Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF) for his failed drugs test and subsequent ban, believing it entered his system while on international duty.
In an interview on Wednesday, Mudryk firmly placed the blame for his 20-month absence from the sport on his national association, which has led to Shevchenko's response.
In a statement, former Chelsea and AC Milan striker Shevchenko, who is now president of the UAF, said Mudryk's comments amounted to a "baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally" and called on the player to retract his words.
He added: "His representatives repeatedly approached the UAF with a proposal to find an employee who would falsely take responsibility for the meldonium found in his doping sample.
"The UAF refused, as such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work."
He added that "numerous investigations and audits" undertaken as part of the case were unable to shed light on when or where the substance entered Mudryk's system.
In his interview Mudryk also claimed Shevchenko had offered him little support, blamed the association for leaks that emerged during the case and said its handling of the matter delayed his return to football.
However, Shevchenko went on to say that national team staff had complied with a request from Chelsea not to provide Mudryk with any medication while on international duty.
And he also challenged the former Shakhtar Donetsk forward to provide evidence "to back up his words".
"Head coach Serhiy Rebrov also approved for Mykhailo to have two of his personal specialists work with him at the training camps," Shevchenko added.
"These were the exact people who monitored his regimen and recovery, and helped him with his daily routine.
"The UAF completed all necessary checks in this case. We provided Mudryk's representatives with the information they requested and remained in contact with those working on the case.
"I know the people who have worked with the national team for many years. I trust them, because throughout all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make anyone doubt their professionalism.
"If Mykhailo has evidence to back up his words, let him provide it. If no such evidence exists, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologise to the people whose honesty and professionalism he has called into question."
BBC Sport has contacted Mudryk's representatives for comment.

The 52-year-old has replaced Stephen Robinson at Pittodrie; the Dons are 11th in the Scottish Premiership; his first game in charge is at Kilmarnock on Saturday; watch Rangers vs Aberdeen on November 24, live on Sky Sports
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Aberdeen's new head coach Mario Frick will not just be happy with Scottish Premiership survival this season, insisting he wants a top-six finish.
The 52-year-old takes over with the side sitting 11th in the table following Stephen Robinson's dismissal after their 4-0 defeat at Hibernian before the international break.
Frick, who played 125 times for Liechtenstein, previously took charge of the national youth teams in his homeland before spells with Vaduz and Luzern, helping the latter to avoid relegation.
"I had a very long career as a professional, so I know the pressure and I'm always optimist," he said.
Asked why he was confident of success, he added: "[Luzern] they were on the bottom of the table with 18 matches and 11 points and the whole environment was sad and we saved them.
"I'm pretty sure we can do this also in this place and I'm very ambitious.
"It's very important to get out of this situation but we want to go in the top six."
Frick will take charge for the first time on Saturday at bottom side Kilmarnock and he is determined to make an immediate impact with his style of football.
"Heavy metal," he said. "That's high pressing, that's counter-pressing vertical play creating many goalscoring chances."
Aberdeen have scored just 12 goals in the league this season while conceding 18 and Frick, who spent most of his playing career as a centre-forward, wants better.
"I'm known for high-scoring clubs. With Vaduz we had the goal record," the former St Gallen player said.
"Everything is lacking to score and so I'm here to change that.
"We have to improve now. We need time but we don't have, so it's more important to show the basics.
"Body language, willing to work, intensity. That's what I want to see."
The Aberdeen supporters booed Robinson off the pitch at the end of what was ultimately his final game at Pittodrie.
With just two home league wins this season, the morale of the Red Army is at a low.
Chief executive Adrian Bevington revealed Frick was the "unanimous decision," although his appointment took most by surprise.
"I'm not here to win with the fans, I'm here to win with my team.
"The supporters are amazing here I know that and but I'm not here to win them. The most important thing is the team and not me."
Frick faces an immediate relegation battle, starting with a run of five fixtures in just 15 days.
His first match is a trip to bottom of the table Kilmarnock. A win would move them five points clear, a defeat would see the Dons drop to 12th.
Next is a tough test against Rangers and former Aberdeen boss Derek McInnes at Ibrox, live on Sky Sports. The Dons have failed to win any of their last eight games against the Gers, losing to them in the Premiership and League Cup already this season.
There is no doubt Frick has taken charge of a team low on confidence, with four straight defeats ultimately leading to his predecessor's dismissal.
He has said he is "very hungry and ready to level up players" and, after playing most of his career as a centre-forward, he wants his team "playing forward and trying to score".
Time is not on the new manager's side. Robinson took four games before his first win, but with the prospect of ending the weekend bottom of the table, Frick will be aiming for a faster start to his Dons career.

Premier League clubs met in central London this morning and voted by 18-2 to provide their board members with indemnity if they are sued individually in any potential defamation suits in light of the independent commission's finding the club entered into 'sham' contracts with sponsors
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Premier League clubs have voted to cover the legal costs of their five board members if they are sued individually by Manchester City's sponsors.
In September, an independent commission found City guilty of breaking more than one hundred of the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018.
City are appealing after the commission found they had entered into "sham" contracts with sponsors.
Two of City's sponsors, Etihad Airways and Etisalat, have threatened the Premier League with legal action.
Premier League clubs met in central London this morning and voted by 18-2 to provide their board members with indemnity if they are sued individually in any potential defamation suits.
City and Nottingham Forest are believed to have voted against. A two-thirds majority - 14 clubs - was required to make the change.
The board members are chair Alison Brittain, chief executive Richard Masters, and non-executive directors Mai Fyfield, Dharmash Mistry and Matthew Ryder.
Abu Dhabi airline Etihad Airways have sponsored City since 2009. In a statement dated 30 September they said the Premier League did not engage with them and they were not given the chance to provide relevant information.
Etihad said it was seeking legal advice to protect their interests. Etihad were not named in the 40-page published decision but they said it had "created damaging implications" for them.
Meanwhile, Abu Dhabi communications company Etisalat says it is are also considering taking legal action against the Premier League.
In a statement, the company said: "Emirates Telecommunications Group Company PJSC (Etisalat) views the published findings of the English Premier League, as they relate to Etisalat, as entirely false and defamatory. Etisalat is actively considering all options relating to its rights and associated legal remedies in this matter."
Sources close to Evangelos Marinakis and the Nottingham Forest board have said their decision to vote alongside Manchester City is in no way meant to show solidarity with a club that has been found guilty of serious financial breaches.
Forest and City were the only clubs who voted against the proposal to share any future legal costs which could be brought by some of City's sponsors who are threatening to sue the Premier League. The vote at the Premier League shareholders meeting was passed 18 votes to two.
Whilst Forest have declined to comment, sources have told Sky Sports News their objection to the proposal is procedural, rather than because of any support for City.
The East Midlands club felt that insufficient information had been provided, and that there wasn't enough time to consider the implications.
Forest felt that such a decision warranted more scrutiny and informed consideration before the matter was put to a vote.
The commission also said it was "regrettable" that a decision had taken so long to reach, with the hearing having taken place between September and December 2024.
A Manchester City statement read: "Manchester City is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League commission that has been published today.
"The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions relating to this case. The club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.
"The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.
"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.
"The club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete."
Manchester City's statement erroneously refers to a Premier League commission. It is an independent commission .

Akol Akon sealed a 2-0 win over football powerhouse in Qatar
Joeys mark return to tournament for first time in seven years
Sydney FC prodigy Akol Akon has demonstrated why he’s one of the most exciting talents in Australian football, leading the Joeys to a shock 2-0 victory over Argentina to launch their U17 World Cup campaign in style.
The brilliant young winger had his shot deflected for an own goal on the hour and then produced an audaciously cheeky finish 11 minutes later to seal the opening-day win on Friday (AEDT) as Carl Veart’s side announced their return to the global boys’ competition for the first time in seven years.
Against one of the powerhouse football nations, Australia had their backs to the wall, having to make 31 clearances as Argentina enjoyed two-thirds of the possession and 22 shots on goal. But the Joeys fought back after the break, spearheaded by Akon, who hailed their second-half heist as “amazing”.
The 17-year-old livewire provided the real star quality, and it was soon evident why the Sky Blues had wanted to keep him in Australia for their A-League Men campaign instead of releasing him for the tournament; a decision that triggered widespread backlash before being reversed.
This article includes content provided by Instagram . We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content, click 'Allow and continue' .
Akon caused havoc from the start down the right flank, his neat through ball in the fifth minute almost resulting in a goal for Central Coast Mariners’ Luke Becvinovski.
The teenage sensation then struck after the break following another dangerous foray down the right that ended with his shot across goal deflecting off the hapless Alvaro Guich and into the net.
In the 71st minute, Mariners midfielder Oli O’Carroll expertly picked off an Argentina attack before Brisbane’s Emmett Shaw released Akon with a slide-rule left-foot pass, the winger going on to dummy the goalkeeper before slotting into an empty net.
It only got worse for Argentina when substitute Benjamin Vallejos got sent off for a reckless challenge in stoppage time.
But it wasn’t all about Akon, a considerable talent who’s already made his national U23 bow. At the other end, Charlie Wilson-Papps, the young goalkeeper who’s on the books at Brighton and Hove Albion, made half-a-dozen fine saves and kept a clean sheet.
“I do it for my teammates, I do it for my family at home, so to make them proud is is the most important thing,” said Akon as he clutched the player-of-the-match trophy afterwards.
Akon’s only worry came with the video checking of his goal. “Ah, that was nerve-racking, man,” he said. “Because at 1-0, it was a very scary game. So to be able to seal it like that, the coach was telling me it was a goal.
“The first goal? It wasn’t really my goal, but I just wanted to do the Tim Cahill, start off the tournament like that. So, yeah, the knee side had to come with it.
“Now, the group, we’re really confident, really confident in our ability, and I think that showed today.”
Next up on Sunday for the Joeys will be Denmark, who lost 4-0 to Mozambique in their Group C opener on Thursday.

The presidents of China, the US and Russia have held an unprecedented summit. While Trump said the three leaders were "making history," Xi described the talks as "fruitful" and Putin called them "open and candid."
Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday for an unprecedented trilateral summit in Shenzhen, bringing together the leaders of the world's three most powerful military powers amid heightened geopolitical tensions.
Xi hailed the talks as "groundbreaking," saying discussions ranged from global governance and denuclearization to the war in Ukraine and energy security.
The "peace declaration" released after their meeting made no mention of Russia's war in Ukraine or the US-led war in Iran.
Instead, the three leaders agreed to pursue reforms of the United Nations, limit the role of the International Criminal Court and reaffirm their commitment to avoiding nuclear war. They also pledged to boost supplies of refined petroleum products to address global energy challenges.
The tightly choreographed meeting fueled concerns that Beijing, Washington and Moscow could seek to reshape the international order around competing spheres of influence.
While Xi said the talks with Trump and Putin were "positive, constructive and fruitful," Trump heralded the gathering as "really making history."
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
For Putin, the three-way talks, and his meetings with both leaders separately earlier, offered a chance to show the world that he was on par with the leaders of the US and China, despite Western efforts to isolate him since he launched the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Emma Chanlett-Avery, senior director for Political-Security Affairs at the Asia Society Policy Institute (ASPI), said Putin had the most to gain from the meeting as "he appeared on the world stage as one of the dominant players in the world."
Chim Lee, a senior analyst with The Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU), echoed this view.
The meeting itself is a "major outcome for Russia," he told DW, pointing to Russian media coverage that has cast it as "reinforcing Russia's standing in the world."
The joint statement also said the leaders are committed to work to reduce nuclear risks and prevent nuclear proliferation.
The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States, known as New START, expired in February.
Trump has said he wants "a new, improved and modernized" deal that includes China.
But Beijing has so far been reluctant to accept limits as its estimated arsenal of around 500 warheads remains far smaller than those of Russia and the US.
Moscow and Washington are believed to possess more than 5,000 warheads each.
Lee said China is unlikely to participate in a trilateral institutionalized setting to control nuclear arms.
"The gap between China's nuclear arsenal and those of Russia and US is still quite large. From China's perspective, it doesn't seem to make a lot of sense to put the three powers in the same bucket in this area."
The expert believes Trump attended the meeting as he is "actively thinking about his legacy in the final two years in office."
"So, in this context, the idea of setting up a trilateral nuclear arms control arrangement would have been a very big achievement," Lee said.
But, in the end, the declaration said the countries would merely engage in "dialogue" on the issue, avoiding any explicit commitments to downsize their nuclear stockpiles.
China initially hesitated to organize the trilateral summit as it did not want to be explicitly tied to Russia's war in Ukraine and harm Beijing's efforts to present itself as a long-term force for global stability.
The Chinese government, which is working to rebalance economic ties with the EU, was also wary of appearing to form a G3 club with Washington and Moscow, which could alienate other global partners.
Chanlett-Avery said that China had some degree of discomfort in convening this meeting, worried about getting involved in Ukraine issues.
But Beijing eventually "managed to get the outcome they wanted" and kept the European conflict out of the meeting's focus, she noted.
"China was able to show off Shenzhen and all of its sparkling high-tech features. They convened a successful international meeting that grabbed lots of headlines," she added. "So, I think China probably came out feeling okay."
Prior to the summit, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had warned of a "second Yalta," referring to the Yalta Conference held in Crimea in 1945.
That meeting saw the Allied powers decide on the post-war European order following the end of World War II.
In Shenzhen, Putin stressed that Russia, the US and China, as victors in World War II and veto-wielding members of the UN Security Council, bore a "joint responsibility for maintaining international peace."
But Ying-Yu Lin, Associate Professor at Graduate Institute of International Affairs and Strategic Studies at Taiwan's Tamkang University, said the Yalta comparison "is a bit of a stretch," given the vast differences between 1945 and now.
Putin also said that all three leaders "agree that it's a useful format," and such meetings could take place again.
Lee, the EIU expert, said the trilateral setup "is unlikely to be just a one-off" and there will probably be more such meetings in the coming years.
"Especially from the US side to have this kind of setup, there will be some interest in maintaining warm relations with both China and Russia," he underlined.

A 12-minute video of Mauricio Pochettino's first training session as Manchester United boss has been leaked online, showing the new head coach doing training drills ahead of Sunday's match against Liverpool at Anfield, which is live on Sky
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session today has been leaked online in a major security breach.
The 12-minute drone footage over their Carrington training ground was uploaded onto YouTube.
It shows Pochettino doing various tactical drills with his new team as they prepare for their clash with Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.
United have signs around the Carrington area warning that use of drones are "strictly prohibited" and anyone caught "will be reported for prosecution and subject to civil action".
The uploaders of the drone footage, CC Overview, claimed to have not breached any laws.
On the video they posted: "For the people asking about legality. It is unrestricted airspace, meaning anyone can fly over it, the drone remained in line of sight at all times, it didn't fly over anyone or even near anyone so was a perfectly legal flight going by the CAA rules that regulates drone usage.
"The drone is correctly labelled and I hold all the relevant licences, public liability and insurance required.
"As for leaking team news/ tactics, it was half an hour into the manager's first training session, there are many media there so certainly won't be the only footage of training released."
The training today was a closed session and not open to the media.
Manchester United declined to comment when contacted by Sky Sports News .
"This 12-minute video starts off innocuously. We see large numbers of Man Utd players on a separate pitch doing what is known as rondos, those small groups of six or seven players with one or two in the middle trying to intercept the ball. It's the classic pre-training warm-up. That's pretty innocuous. That won't give Liverpool or anyone else much of an insight into what Pochettino's tactical thinking might be for his first game in charge.
"But then on the next pitch, as the drone moves across, it zooms in, and the zoom is quite incredible. You can make out faces and we see Pochettino hands-on, walking them through certain match scenarios. At one stage Pochettino calls all those players in for a huddle and a briefing.
"I'm not going to give you any information about who those players are. But these 11 players Pochettino calls in - 10 outfield players and one goalkeeper. We shouldn't assume this is his starting XI, necessarily.
"Saturday would be the day we'd expect United to do their specific tactics and shape to prepare for the game at Anfield the next day. If this was drone footage of that session it would be even more damaging, even more explosive.
"But the fact it's 11 players separated from the group... it's a very difficult situation for Pochettino and Manchester United.
"I don't think [Pochettino and the players] were aware of it at the time.
"It's questionable whether the person handling the drone has done anything illegal. All around Carrington training ground, they have a large numbers of signs up saying drones are prohibited. But it's clear from these images the drone was not flying directly above United's property. It was to the side of United's property and zoomed in.
"There's absolutely no suggestion Liverpool are involved in this, they are clearly not. But you have to say, it could be advantageous to Liverpool and Andoni Iraola if he's planning his tactics for Sunday's game to look at this and get an idea of how Manchester United might be lining up and what Pochettino might be thinking.
"While it seems as though there are probably no laws that have been broken here, nevertheless it's an awful lot of very specific footage which Manchester United and Pochettino would not want out in the public.
"If you look at the impact of what we're talking about, Man Utd earlier today released some images of the training session and it showed Harry Maguire and Patrick Dorgu among the main training group. Both of those have had injury concerns of late. So those official images told me, Man Utd supporters and Liverpool's tactical preparation experts that Maguire and Dorgu may be in line for possible selection.
"It's gone a stage further now with this leaked drone footage because that has shed even more light on that. It gives a pretty clear picture of who's fit, who's out on the training field, who's involved and who isn't.
"That has to be a significant tactical advantage to Andoni Iraola and Liverpool as they go into this huge game on Sunday."
